name: Incident Response Process
description: Enforces incident response runbook patterns for identifying, responding to, and learning from production incidents.
content:
# Incident Response Process Rules

- Define severity levels with clear criteria — S1 (complete outage), S2 (degraded service), S3 (minor impact), S4 (no user impact)
- Establish an on-call rotation — every production service needs a responsible person reachable 24/7
- When an incident is detected, open an incident channel immediately — centralize communication in one place
- Assign clear roles — Incident Commander (coordinates), Technical Lead (debugs), Communications Lead (updates stakeholders)
- Prioritize mitigation over root cause — restore service first (rollback, failover, scale up), investigate later
- Communicate status updates every 15-30 minutes during active incidents — even if the update is "still investigating"
- Maintain a public status page — users should be able to check service status without contacting support
- Document timeline of events during the incident — when it started, what was tried, when it was resolved
- Conduct blameless postmortems for S1 and S2 incidents — focus on systemic improvements, not individual blame
- Postmortems must include — summary, impact, timeline, root cause, what went well, what went poorly, action items
- Track action items from postmortems to completion — assign owners and deadlines, review in team meetings
- Practice incident response — run game days or chaos engineering exercises to test your processes before real incidents
